content.title: About
content.content: Clif Bar is a whole-food energy bar designed for active people and athletes. It contains whole grains, nuts, dried fruit, plant‑based protein, and added vitamins and minerals to support energy and recovery.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first Clif Bar was created in 1992 in California as a "cyclist’s energy snack".
Most varieties contain organic rolled oats that provide a slow‑release source of carbohydrates.
The bars are free from artificial flavors, colors, and GMOs.
Clif Bar offers more than 20 flavors, including chocolate, berry, and nut blends.
Each bar is packaged in recyclable material, and the company supports environmental stewardship programs.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: Complex carbs from whole grains and fruit deliver a steady flow of glucose during prolonged activity.

items.title: Plant protein
items.content: Bars provide 9–11 g of protein per serving, helping muscle repair after exercise.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Added B1, B2, B3, and B6 support carbohydrate metabolism and boost endurance.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Approximately 3 g of fiber per bar promotes healthy digestion and prolonged satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Calcium, iron, and magnesium contribute to bone health and muscle function.

items.title: Nut and soy allergy
items.content: Some varieties contain nuts, peanuts, or soy protein, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Bars contain 12–18 g of sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: One bar provides about 250 kcal, which can contribute to weight gain if consumed excessively.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Certain flavors include wheat, making them unsuitable for a gluten‑free diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is convenient to take to the gym, on a hike, or during travel. Eat it 10–15 minutes before a workout for fuel or right after for recovery. You can also slice the bar and add it to yogurt, oatmeal, or a smoothie.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal the package tightly or transfer the bar to an airtight container to maintain its crunchy texture.
